script to redo plotting of Tage for geroscreen that nick computed 

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## ARI GeroScreen — transcriptomic age (tAge) clocks
## Input : tAge_GeroScreen_vehicle_cell_line.csv
##         (per-sample tAge_Chronoage and tAge_Mortality, relative values)

## ---- 0. Setup ---------------------------------------------------------------
setwd("/restricted/projectnb/crem-trainees/Murphy_Lab/Elise/GeroScreen_Paper")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

## The file contains "µ" in the concentration column, saved in Latin-1 encoding
tage_raw <- read.csv("tAge_GeroScreen_vehicle_cell_line.csv",
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "latin1")

out_dir <- "tAge_figures"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

base_font <- "sans"

## Values in the file are already relative. Set TRUE to additionally subtract
## each line's vehicle mean, so vehicle sits exactly at 0 in both lines.
center_on_vehicle <- FALSE

## ---- 1. Sample annotation ---------------------------------------------------
group_levels <- c("CTRL", "RUT", "SIT", "GEN", "EBS", "CAL", "PI", "TRA", "RAP")
treatments   <- setdiff(group_levels, "CTRL")

## Same colours as every other panel (Okabe-Ito, grey for vehicle)
group_cols <- setNames(c("grey55", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
                         "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"),
                       group_levels)

## Group taken from the sample name (e.g. "BU6_RUT1" -> "RUT")
tage <- tage_raw %>%
  mutate(line  = factor(cell_line),
         group = factor(sub("[0-9]+$", "", sub("^[^_]+_", "", sample_name)),
                        levels = group_levels))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(tage$group)))
print(table(tage$group, tage$line))

metrics <- c(tAge_Chronoage = "Chronological tAge",
             tAge_Mortality = "Mortality tAge")
y_labels <- c("Chronological tAge" = "Relative chronological tAge (years)",
              "Mortality tAge"     = "Relative mortality tAge")

tage_long <- tage %>%
  select(sample_name, line, group, all_of(names(metrics))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(metrics)), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metrics[metric], levels = metrics))

if (center_on_vehicle) {
  tage_long <- tage_long %>%
    group_by(metric, line) %>%
    mutate(value = value - mean(value[group == "CTRL"])) %>%
    ungroup()
}

write.csv(tage_long, file.path(out_dir, "tAge_values_long.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 2. Statistics: value ~ group + line, each treatment vs vehicle ----------
tage_stats <- tage_long %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    m  <- summary(lm(value ~ group + line, data = .x))$coefficients
    rn <- paste0("group", treatments)
    data.frame(treatment = treatments,
               estimate  = m[rn, "Estimate"],
               se        = m[rn, "Std. Error"],
               P.Value   = m[rn, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  }) %>%
  mutate(adj.P.Val = p.adjust(P.Value, method = "BH")) %>%  # across 8 treatments
  ungroup()
write.csv(tage_stats, file.path(out_dir, "tAge_stats_vs_vehicle.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p_to_star <- function(p) {
  as.character(cut(p, breaks = c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf),
                   labels = c("***", "**", "*", ""), right = FALSE))
}

## Star positions: just above the highest point in each facet/group
star_df <- tage_long %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  mutate(rng = diff(range(value))) %>%
  group_by(metric, group) %>%
  summarise(y = max(value) + 0.12 * first(rng), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(tage_stats %>%
               transmute(metric, group = factor(treatment, levels = group_levels),
                         label = p_to_star(adj.P.Val)),
             by = c("metric", "group"))

## ---- 3. Plot (same style as the mTORC1 / MEK-ERK score figure) ---------------
theme_screen <- theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = base_font) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
        strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position    = "right")

make_tage_plot <- function(dat, stars, y_lab, title, subtitle) {
  ggplot(dat, aes(group, value)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.25) +
    stat_summary(aes(colour = group), fun = mean, geom = "crossbar",
                 width = 0.5, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = group, shape = line), size = 2,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
    geom_text(data = stars, aes(y = y, label = label), size = 5) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = "Line") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab, title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_screen
}

stat_subtitle <- "Stars = lm(value ~ group + line) vs CTRL, BH-adjusted across treatments"

## Combined figure: both clocks side by side
p_both <- make_tage_plot(tage_long, star_df,
                         y_lab = "Relative tAge",
                         title = "Transcriptomic age (tAge)",
                         subtitle = stat_subtitle)

## Individual figures
p_chrono <- make_tage_plot(filter(tage_long, metric == "Chronological tAge"),
                           filter(star_df, metric == "Chronological tAge"),
                           y_lab = y_labels["Chronological tAge"],
                           title = "Chronological tAge",
                           subtitle = stat_subtitle)
p_mort   <- make_tage_plot(filter(tage_long, metric == "Mortality tAge"),
                           filter(star_df, metric == "Mortality tAge"),
                           y_lab = y_labels["Mortality tAge"],
                           title = "Mortality tAge",
                           subtitle = stat_subtitle)

## ---- 4. Save (cairo for both PNG and PDF) ------------------------------------
save_fig <- function(p, name, w, h) {
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = w, height = h,
         units = "in", dpi = 600, device = png, type = "cairo")
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h,
         units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
}
save_fig(p_both,   "tAge_chrono_and_mortality", 9,   4.5)
save_fig(p_chrono, "tAge_chronological",        5.5, 4.5)
save_fig(p_mort,   "tAge_mortality",            5.5, 4.5)

## ---- 5. Session info ----------------------------------------------------------
## ---- 5. Per-line figure: each clock x each cell line ------------------------
## Rows = clock, columns = cell line. Each row shares one y-axis across BU6 and
## BU8 so the two lines can be compared directly. No stars here: within one
## line there are only 2 technical replicates per compound, too few for a
## meaningful test (the line-adjusted statistics are in the combined figure).
tage_line <- tage_long %>%
  mutate(line = factor(line, levels = c("BU6", "BU8")))
 
p_by_line <- ggplot(tage_line, aes(group, value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.25) +
  stat_summary(aes(colour = group), fun = mean, geom = "crossbar",
               width = 0.5, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group, shape = line), size = 2,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ line, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(BU6 = 16, BU8 = 17), guide = "none") +  # panels already labelled by line
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative tAge",
       title = "Transcriptomic age by cell line",
       subtitle = "Mean \u00b1 SEM of 2 technical replicates per compound") +
  theme_screen
 
save_fig(p_by_line, "tAge_by_cell_line", 9, 7)

## ---- 6. Per-line figure: chronological tAge only -----------------------------
## BU6 and BU8 side by side, shared y-axis, same style as section 5
p_chrono_by_line <- ggplot(filter(tage_line, metric == "Chronological tAge"),
                           aes(group, value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.25) +
  stat_summary(aes(colour = group), fun = mean, geom = "crossbar",
               width = 0.5, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group, shape = line), size = 2,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ line, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(BU6 = 16, BU8 = 17), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative chronological tAge (years)",
       title = "Chronological tAge by cell line",
       subtitle = "Mean \u00b1 SEM of 2 technical replicates per compound") +
  theme_screen
 
save_fig(p_chrono_by_line, "tAge_chronological_by_cell_line", 9, 4.5)
```
